issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): the problem statement's UML (problem_statement.md) declares getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning an int, but the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) defines getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and provides a StudentCount class (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StudentCount.java). The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) contains a TODO for this method and does not define a StudentCount type or a concrete signature. This mismatch leaves students unsure whether to implement an int-returning method (as the UML says) or a StudentCount-returning method (as the solution does), which can cause confusion and inconsistent implementations or compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Two valid resolutions: (A) Align with the UML/problem text: change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and update dependent methods (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()) to use int; remove StudentCount from the solution and do not add it to the template. Update solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java accordingly. OR (B) Adopt the StudentCount wrapper as authoritative: update problem_statement.md and the UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and add StudentCount.java to the template_repository (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/) and provide the method signature in the template's Lecture.java so students implement the same type. Document the chosen design in the problem text. Either fix ensures students have a single, unambiguous expected return type and a compilable template.
